ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv

meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester

to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  June 11, 2024

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
June 11, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney
  Destinee Wesley  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel
present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
Authority.

Mayor Butts introduced the new Interim City Attorney, Rick R. Olivarez.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.

There was no response.
 June 11, 2024

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS – RECEIVED AND FILED. The demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June 6, 2024, in
  the amount of $4,991,937.14, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are received and filed.

  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman ordered the Warrants and
  Bills received and filed.

 142  BLANKET PURCHASE ORDER NO. 24-248 APPROVED – AMAZON SERVICES,
  LLC dba AMAZON BUSINESS. Staff report dated June 11, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve a blanket purchase order with
  Amazon Services, LLC, dba Amazon Business through January 28, 2026, (with the option
  to extend two additional years).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve blanket purchase order No. 24-248 in an amount not
  to exceed $250,000, annually. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 23-219 APPROVED – TRIO
  COMMUNITY MEALS, LLC. Staff report dated June 11, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No. 1 to
  Agreement No. 23-219 with TRIO Community Meals, LLC, extending the term of the
  agreement by one year, in an annual amount not to exceed $202,134.90.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 23-219. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AMENDMENT APPROVED – COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES WORKFORCE
  DEVELOPMENT AGING AND COMMUNITY SERVICES (WDACS). Staff report
  dated June 11, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  approve Amendment Sixteen of the Elderly Nutrition Program Services Subaward Number
  ENP202107 (City Agreement No. 20-201) with County of Los Angeles Workforce
  Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to receive additional funding for
  the Elderly Nutrition Program, in the amount of $357,000.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby Approve Amendment Sixteen. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

160  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 23-228 APPROVED – LPA, INC. Staff
  report dated June 11, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 23-228 with LPA, Inc.,
  (“Architect”) for $989,480 in additional architectural and engineering services for the Main
  Library Renovation.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 23-228;
  and 2) Approve an increase to the 10% City Controlled Contingency, in the amount of
  $98,948, for a new contingency amount not to exceed $362,700, resulting in a new total
  project amount not to exceed $3,989,700. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

  2
 June 11, 2024

  Noes: None.
131.8  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – RSG, INC. Staff report dated June 11, 2024, was
  presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members authorize payment to RSG,
  Inc. for affordable housing consultant services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Gray that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $12,147.50. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 24-250 APPROVED – LOS ANGELES ORGANIZING
  COMMITTEE. Staff report dated June 11, 2024, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members approve an agreement between the City of Inglewood and the
  Los Angeles Organizing Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Games 2028 (LA28).

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that the City
  Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 24-250. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION - MERCURY INSURANCE
  COMPANY V. CITY OF INGLEWOOD; LASC CASE NO. 24STLC00117. Closed
  Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal
  Counsel regarding anticipated litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(2); Mercury Insurance Company v. City of Inglewood; LASC Case No.
  24STLC00117.

  Direction Given; No Action Taken.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, welcomed the new City
  Attorney, Rick Olivarez. She stated that she was happy to see him and she heard great things
  about him. The City Clerk also stated she looked forward to working with him and
  congratulated him again. She wished the fathers a happy Father’s Day and added that they
  are the best, appreciated, loved, and thanked them for all that they do.

126  MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated June 11, 2024, was presented
  submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the Month ending April 30, 2024.

  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the honor of David and Hector Sayatt, Reverend James Lawson, and Tonia
  Haro, at the hour of 2:27 p.m.

  Approved this 27th day of August, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor

 June 11, 2024
